purpose: Offline business reference and visible demonstration explanation; not a runtime interpreter, prompt, validator, training update or new evaluation bank.
question: What currently pays for your everyday living costs?
review_limit: Annotations were authored from existing evidence; no independent human business sign-off is claimed.
case_status: Existing opened fictional examples, already used for development and repair; not unseen evaluation.
interpretation_boundary: Gold fields are copied unchanged from the saved expectations. Business annotations and proposed wording are offline explanatory material, not model requests or accepted runtime financial facts.
nonclear_boundary: For missing_information, do not force an exact raw bucket. For undecided/confusion, keep option and financial facts empty in the runtime contract. Supported facts listed here do not override that requirement.

cases.text: My wages stay in savings. My pension pays the bills.

gold.meaning: Pension pays bills; wages are retained, not spent.
gold.next: Confirm pension and exclusion of wages.

sources.note: Explicitly retained; do not count receiving or saving wages as current spending.

business_annotations.category_reason: One active category: pension payments. Mentioning wages does not make this MULTIPLE.

cases.proposed_follow_up: Your pension pays the bills, while your wages stay in savings. Have I understood correctly?

cases.text: Both my wages and pension pay for everyday costs.

gold.meaning: Salary and pension both currently pay costs.

sources.evidence_quote: Both my wages and pension pay for everyday costs.
sources.note: The sentence explicitly links both categories to current costs.

sources.evidence_quote: Both my wages and pension pay for everyday costs.
sources.note: The shared quotation supports a second, different category.

business_annotations.category_reason: Two different active funding categories support D5_MULTIPLE.

cases.proposed_follow_up: Both your wages and pension payments pay your everyday costs. Have I understood correctly?

cases.text: Pay from my two employers covers my living costs.

gold.meaning: Two employers fund costs; one salary category, not multiple categories.

sources.evidence_quote: Pay from my two employers covers my living costs.
sources.note: Two payers share one salary category and one current-use relationship.

business_annotations.category_reason: Count funding categories, not employers: this is salary only, not D5_MULTIPLE.

cases.proposed_follow_up: Pay from your two employers covers your living costs. That is one salary or wages category. Have I understood correctly?

cases.text: Benefits and regular help from my family pay my bills.

gold.meaning: Benefits and family help are distinct sources in one category.

sources.evidence_quote: Benefits and regular help from my family pay my bills.
sources.note: Both sources belong to the existing benefits or regular support category.

business_annotations.category_reason: Two kinds of support share one approved category; do not select D5_MULTIPLE or reject a repeated payer.

cases.proposed_follow_up: Benefits and regular help from your family pay your bills. Have I understood correctly?

cases.text: My brother sends me money every week for rent and food.

gold.meaning: Customer receives regular support for living costs; do not classify brother's earnings.

sources.evidence_quote: My brother sends me money every week for rent and food.
sources.note: Classify support received by the customer. The brother's underlying earnings are not stated or required.

business_annotations.category_reason: Regular support for rent and food is one benefits or support category.

cases.proposed_follow_up: Your brother sends you money every week for rent and food. Have I understood correctly?

cases.text: I use my savings for bills. My pension starts next year.

gold.meaning: Current savings withdrawals fund bills; pension is future and excluded.
gold.next: Confirm withdrawals without asking irrelevant future-pension details.

sources.evidence_quote: I use my savings for bills.
sources.note: The use of savings is explicit; do not claim investment withdrawals were mentioned.
Future pension payments do not fund current costs.

business_annotations.category_reason: One current withdrawals category, specifically savings. Future pension payments do not make this MULTIPLE.

cases.proposed_follow_up: You use your savings for bills, and your pension starts next year. Have I understood correctly?

cases.text: I have a pension fund, but I have not started drawing from it.

gold.meaning: Undrawn pension holding establishes no active source. Other funding is not known; not no regular source.
gold.next: Ask what currently pays living costs; do not infer that the customer misunderstands or is undecided.

sources.evidence_quote: I have a pension fund, but I have not started drawing from it.
sources.note: The category is the payment category being considered, not a claim that holding a fund produces payments. No current drawing is established.

business_annotations.category_reason: An excluded pension holding does not identify the source that actually pays costs, or establish no regular source.
missing_facts: Which sources, if any, currently pay living costs

cases.proposed_follow_up: What currently pays your everyday living costs? You can name another source or say if you do not have a regular source.

cases.text: I have no regular source paying my living costs at the moment.

gold.meaning: Explicit current absence of a regular funding source, not absence of assets.

business_annotations.category_reason: The user explicitly states no regular source currently pays living costs. This does not say that they have no assets.

cases.proposed_follow_up: You currently have no regular source paying your living costs. Have I understood correctly?

cases.text: I receive wages and pension payments

gold.meaning: Receipt of wages and pension alone does not establish spending; do not default to multiple or customer indecision.
gold.next: Ask which sources actually fund costs now, allowing another source or neither.

sources.evidence_quote: I receive wages and pension payments
sources.note: Receipt is stated; expenditure is not.

sources.evidence_quote: I receive wages and pension payments
sources.note: Receipt is stated; expenditure is not.

business_annotations.category_reason: Two received income categories do not establish two active cost-funding categories. Do not guess MULTIPLE, no regular source or customer indecision.
missing_facts: Whether wages pay current living costs
Whether pension payments pay current living costs
Whether another source, or no regular source, instead pays these costs

cases.proposed_follow_up: Which sources currently pay your everyday living costs: your wages, your pension payments, both, or something else? It is fine to say neither or that this is still unclear.

cases.text: My pension pays some bills; I cannot tell whether my wages also do.

gold.meaning: Customer explicitly cannot establish whether wages also pay costs; no financial facts/option in nonclear contract output.
gold.next: Neutral question focused on wage use; allow unresolved, avoid a generic menu alone.

sources.note: This supported relationship is an offline business annotation only; do not put financial facts in a nonclear model output.

sources.evidence_quote: I cannot tell whether my wages also do.
sources.note: The customer explicitly cannot establish wage use, so the gold kind is Undecided.

business_annotations.category_reason: Do not silently reduce this to pension only or assume MULTIPLE. The complete answer remains unresolved.
missing_facts: Whether wages also currently pay any living costs

cases.proposed_follow_up: It is fine to be unsure. Do your wages also pay any of your living costs, or is that still unclear?

cases.text: Does pension mean my fund or payments?

gold.meaning: Terminology question, no personal financial assertion; no financial facts/option.
gold.next: Explain current payments used for bills versus a pension holding. If pre-model Help handles it, report dialogue success with zero interpretation calls, not model success.

business_annotations.category_reason: This is a question about terminology, not an assertion of personal pension ownership or payments.
missing_facts: Understanding the distinction between a pension holding and payments used for costs

cases.proposed_follow_up: Here, pension means payments you currently receive and use for living costs. Simply holding money in a pension fund does not count. What currently pays your everyday living costs?
